question_vi: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) là gì? Cách cải thiện LCP?
question_en: What is LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)? How do you improve LCP?
answer_vi: LCP đo thời điểm render phần tử lớn nhất trong viewport — thường là hero image, block text lớn hoặc video poster. Good <2.5s, poor >4s. Cách cải thiện: - **Cải thiện TTFB trước** — server response time, CDN, edge caching; TTFB là phần nền của mọi LCP. - **Tối ưu ảnh** — serve WebP/AVIF (nhỏ hơn JPEG 25–50%), đúng kích thước container, responsive `srcset`. - **Preload LCP image** — `` trong `` + `fetchpriority='high'` để browser ưu tiên fetch sớm. - **Không lazy-load LCP image** — `loading='lazy'` trên hero image làm LCP tăng đáng kể; chỉ lazy-load below-fold. - **Loại bỏ render-blocking resources** — defer/async JS không critical, inline critical CSS, preconnect third-party domains. - **Next.js `next/image`** — tự convert format, responsive size, lazy mặc định; thêm prop `priority` cho LCP image. Lỗi hay gặp: LCP image đặt bằng CSS `background-image` bị discover trễ (browser phải parse xong CSS) — dùng `` cho LCP element.
answer_en: LCP measures the render time of the largest element in the viewport — typically a hero image, a large text block, or a video poster. Good <2.5s, poor >4s. How to improve: - **Improve TTFB first** — server response time, CDN, edge caching; TTFB is the floor under every LCP. - **Optimize images** — serve WebP/AVIF (25–50% smaller than JPEG), size to the container, responsive `srcset`. - **Preload the LCP image** — `` in `` + `fetchpriority='high'` so the browser fetches it early. - **Never lazy-load the LCP image** — `loading='lazy'` on a hero image significantly increases LCP; only lazy-load below-fold content. - **Eliminate render-blocking resources** — defer/async non-critical JS, inline critical CSS, preconnect to third-party domains. - **Next.js `next/image`** — automatic format conversion, responsive sizes, lazy by default; add the `priority` prop for the LCP image. Common pitfall: an LCP image set via CSS `background-image` is discovered late (the browser must parse CSS first) — use `` for the LCP element
answer_html_vi:
LCP đo thời điểm render phần tử lớn nhất trong viewport — thường là hero image, block text lớn hoặc video poster. Good <2.5s, poor >4s.

Cách cải thiện:
- Cải thiện TTFB trước — server response time, CDN, edge caching; TTFB là phần nền của mọi LCP.
- Tối ưu ảnh — serve WebP/AVIF (nhỏ hơn JPEG 25–50%), đúng kích thước container, responsive srcset.
- Preload LCP image — <link rel='preload' as='image' href='hero.webp'> trong <head> + fetchpriority='high' để browser ưu tiên fetch sớm.
- Không lazy-load LCP image — loading='lazy' trên hero image làm LCP tăng đáng kể; chỉ lazy-load below-fold.
- Loại bỏ render-blocking resources — defer/async JS không critical, inline critical CSS, preconnect third-party domains.
- Next.js next/image — tự convert format, responsive size, lazy mặc định; thêm prop priority cho LCP image.

Lỗi hay gặp: LCP image đặt bằng CSS background-image bị discover trễ (browser phải parse xong CSS) — dùng <img> cho LCP element.
answer_html_en:
LCP measures the render time of the largest element in the viewport — typically a hero image, a large text block, or a video poster. Good <2.5s, poor >4s.

How to improve:
- Improve TTFB first — server response time, CDN, edge caching; TTFB is the floor under every LCP.
- Optimize images — serve WebP/AVIF (25–50% smaller than JPEG), size to the container, responsive srcset.
- Preload the LCP image — <link rel='preload' as='image' href='hero.webp'> in <head> + fetchpriority='high' so the browser fetches it early.
- Never lazy-load the LCP image — loading='lazy' on a hero image significantly increases LCP; only lazy-load below-fold content.
- Eliminate render-blocking resources — defer/async non-critical JS, inline critical CSS, preconnect to third-party domains.
- Next.js next/image — automatic format conversion, responsive sizes, lazy by default; add the priority prop for the LCP image.

Common pitfall: an LCP image set via CSS background-image is discovered late (the browser must parse CSS first) — use <img> for the LCP element.
